evidence: src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: createApp(Controllers) only registers routes that call OrderController/StockController methods, plus notFoundHandler and errorHandler.
src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: parsePlaceOrderBody and parseStateQuery only check the shape of request input; the doc comment says 'business rules are enforced by the domain'.
src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: parseStateQuery uses the domain's isOrderStatus instead of copying the list of order states.
src/infrastructure/http/requestParsing.ts: throws ValidationError so failures go to the shared errorHandler that createApp.ts registers.
Graph: OrderController.ts imports requestParsing.ts, so the parsers are used inside the same HTTP adapter.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This unit passes. Both files deal with one concern: the HTTP delivery adapter. createApp.ts sets up the Express app and its routes, and hands each request to the controllers and middleware. requestParsing.ts checks the shape of untrusted request input and turns it into application commands or domain types. Its parsers are used by OrderController in the same HTTP adapter. No invariant is copied. Order-status validity comes from the domain's isOrderStatus rather than being re-coded, and the doc comment says business rules stay in the domain. Validation failures use the domain's ValidationError, so they reach the shared errorHandler instead of the parser writing HTTP responses itself. Nothing goes around the module's own pieces: routes call controller methods, and the 404 and error handlers come from the middleware.
